R297-001's explicit-target layout and poisoned round-one stamp are repaired. This verdict replaces performance's prior-head BLOCK only. New final-round P297-R2-001 ships as F246 under the prime's C34 ruling relayed by pm-001: invalidate and warn if stamp publication fails, folded into falcon's F245 PR. It is not fixed at this head; no third review round. F226's release-build --version == HEAD check is a deployment backstop, not proof every generic shared-build result is correct.

Scope and invariants:
- R2 commits e928ead0,56a9dfd0,51984328 repair the scan/state/stamp publication. Main merge a315839d brings #295/50254c01, independently reviewed; its F245 and held sweep --apply are not cleared here. Against main50254c01 this PR remains7files291+/35-. F244 bounce code is unchanged from the reviewed first-round scope.
- shared-build.sh386-394: only exact 'finished <this worktree>' can reuse without a touch, subject to the newer-artifact scan. Missing/foreign/running or round-one bare stamps force invalidation. The first corrected run therefore does not trust a false-success round-one stamp newer than foreign artifacts.
- The scan has no depth limit: native profile/deps and triple/profile/deps layouts are covered; it prunes entries named build, incremental and .fingerprint, and stops on the first newer deps entry. It traverses other nonpruned directories, not only deps. No subprocess per entry.
- The existing target lock encloses read/scan/touch, 'running' publication before cargo, each command and its child drain, 'finished' publication only after all commands, and copy-out. Normally a failed or cut-short batch leaves running, so the next caller touches even if that batch wrote outside deps. Ordinary same-tree successful reuse remains possible.

Cost/backpressure:
| Site | Work per acquired batch | Scaling/limit |
|---|---|---|
| artifact scan | zero or one /usr/bin/find; OR short-circuits unless finished stamp names this tree | O(unpruned entries visited), arbitrary depth and count; no fixed wall-time ceiling |
| successful existing-target stamp publication | TWO /usr/bin/mktemp + TWO /bin/mv | running and finished; builtins for comparisons/read/printf; once per batch, not per cargo command |
| failed batch after running publication | one mktemp + one mv, no finished publication | publication error can add /bin/rm cleanup; no retry loop |
| source invalidation | existing one conditional touch over crate roots | O(workspace roots) only on invalidation; repeat reuse avoids full rebuild |
| unchanged F244 helper failure | nominal10 absolute /bin/sleep0.1 launches/s for additional1–2s integerSECONDS wait | about<=20 sleeps after initial helper timeout only; no per-seat/steady-daemon cadence |

No new daemon loop/timer/launch site. Existing shared-target waiting20s df/mkdir/sleep, nice19/job caps, cargo child drains and daemon spawn inventory remain unchanged. No work at rest; cost scales with build invocations/target contents, not seats. Missing tmux launches no guard helper, but build/install/npm/lsof already occurred; refusal leaves old daemon running, not installed bytes unchanged. The stamp decision is a correctness POLICY; forcing a rebuild is the conservative outcome, not permission to hide a wrong binary as a speedup.

This is the full-negative case on that fixed tree, not a universal50ms maximum, all filesystem entries counted, or a performance-seat rerun.
Earlier native release-build receipts /tmp/f243-receipts.md, /tmp/f243-rb.err and /tmp/f243-other.err remain prior-revision coder measurements: repeats1–2s/0crate compiles; final raw release0.78s; foreign-tree raw11compiles/1m19s; returning-A83s/11 survives only as summary. First81s 'no stamp' label was corrected: sources were newer, stamp already present. No final-head release timing or new fleet savings is claimed.

F246 / publication boundary:
shared-build.sh375-382 deliberately treats stamp creation/publication as best-effort: mktemp failure returns0 and write/move failure cleans up without independently refusing cargo. [INFERENCE] an old finished mark can survive failure to publish running, so the marker guarantee is conditional on successful publication; the all-deps scan remains the fallback, not proof for arbitrary outputs outside deps. No publication-failure wrong executable was observed by this seat or induced by the reviewer. Prime explicitly accepted F246 (invalidate and warn) as a nonblocking residual; F226 checks copied release binary version against HEAD before install. Do not equate that backstop with unconditional generic cache correctness.
Security's precheck for symlink/directory stamp paths skips publication and forces repeated touches; exclusive temp creation and rename add the two publication pairs above. The same-user check/rename window is disclosed under C33 and belongs to security's clearance; no security guarantee beyond the examined source is asserted.

Proof and limitations:
Exact source HEAD/diff, relevant unchanged lock/copy-out, and final regression source inspected. bash -n harness/scripts/shared-build.sh at this head exited0. Requester's FINAL/CI5of5 is not a performance rerun. Coder26/26 and R1-R4/MS1-MS3/SL mutation outcomes are retained summary receipts, not an independently rerun suite or full raw vitest transcript. The diagnostic scan_found_newer field in those runners still invokes the old depth3 probe, so it is not evidence about the corrected find; the real executable and marker outcomes are the oracles.
Independently inspected termite's exact51984328 real-Cargo runner/raw at /Users/jordanknight/.copilot/session-state/92e8155b-d900-4be5-9dbf-221f3d77669f/files/pr297-r2-explicit-target-probe.{mjs,log}. This is the same consumer-visible oracle that failed at the earlier head, not an mtime-only echo or a repeat production build. It establishes R297-001 closure for the exercised explicit target and adoption path, not F246 publication-error behavior.
